name: Transwestern Phoenix Lateral

values.OtherEnglishNames: TW Phoenix Lateral Project; Phoenix Lateral

researcher_notes: Not an existing row: the Transwestern rows in the roster are P0273 (main line) and P7840 (Desert Southwest Expansion, proposed), and nothing mentions Phoenix. Completed expansion that added new pipe well over 25 km, so it meets the length rule and gets its own row under the parent system name. The EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects August 2026 release, sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel row 588, lists TW Phoenix Lateral Project, operator Transwestern Pipeline Co, completed 20 February 2009, 284 miles, 24/36/42 inch, 500 MMcf/d additional capacity, cost 957 million dollars, FERC docket CP06-459, state AZ. An Oil and Gas Journal article from 1 October 2007 on the FERC final environmental impact statement says about 260 miles of 42 and 36 inch pipe in Arizona plus 25 miles of 36 inch pipe in New Mexico, and names Phoenix as the destination. The two sources differ on length (285 miles proposed, 284 miles in EIA after completion); the EIA figure is staged. EIA lists 24 inch too, which the article does not mention; staged 36,42 only. Start location near Ash Fork on the mainline comes only from the earlier candidate note and was not confirmed in a source, so start fields are left blank. The FERC order for CP06-459 was not opened, so the two sources are EIA and a trade article about the FERC document. Route not researched. Check whether the 4345 km on P0273 already includes this lateral. Capacity is incremental.
